seo_description: Free, open-source macOS toolbox for JSON, Base64, JWT, hashes and timestamps. Paste and Detect picks the right tool from your clipboard. Fully offline.
hero_sub: DevScrapToolbox formats JSON, decodes JWTs, hashes files and converts timestamps, all offline. Press Shift-Command-V and it opens the right tool; Control-Option-Space summons it from anywhere.
features_sub: Each tool has an input pane, an output pane and a copy button, so the common conversions take seconds.

features.title: Paste and Detect
features.desc: Reads your clipboard, guesses whether it is JSON, a JWT, a timestamp, URL-encoded or Base64, and opens the matching tool with the content already filled in.

features.title: JSON with exact error positions
features.desc: Pretty-print with sorted keys or minify. Invalid input reports the line and column, and large files are processed off the main thread with a progress indicator.

features.title: JWT decoder that stays honest
features.desc: Shows header and payload as readable JSON, converts exp, iat and nbf to dates and flags expired tokens. It states clearly that the signature is not verified.

features.title: Hashes, UUIDs, timestamps, case
features.desc: MD5, SHA1, SHA256 and SHA512 of text or a dropped file, up to 10,000 UUIDs at once, seconds or milliseconds timestamps in local and UTC, and camel, snake, kebab or upper case.

features.title: Global hotkey and menu bar
features.desc: Bring up the window from any app with a hotkey you choose in Settings, or use the menu bar item for Open, Paste and Detect, Settings and Support.

features.title: Offline by design
features.desc: No network calls, no analytics and no third-party dependencies. Only Apple frameworks, and your data never leaves your Mac.

faq.q: Is DevScrapToolbox really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license and the full source is on GitHub. If it saves you time, there is an optional Support button in Settings and the menu bar.
None. It does not use Accessibility, Screen Recording or Microphone access. It reads the clipboard only when you use Paste and Detect or when auto-detect is on, which you can turn off in Settings.
Nothing you paste is saved or sent anywhere. Only your preferences, such as hotkey and font size, are stored locally on your Mac.

faq.q: Why is the app not notarized?
faq.a: Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source with Xcode and XcodeGen.
